note: English B2 reading rounds in the Cambridge B2 First format (Reading and Use of English; owner's plan 2026-10-30). Parts 1–7: multiple-choice cloze ×8, open cloze ×8 (typed), word formation ×8 (typed), key word transformations ×6 (typed, two to five words), a long text ×6, a gapped text (six of seven sentences), multiple matching ×10 (four sections). Original texts. Drafted in tools/.mockups/en_b2.py.

items.text:
Is a four-day week the future?
A growing number of companies are (1) ＿＿＿＿＿ with a four-day working week. Supporters (2) ＿＿＿＿＿ that employees who work fewer hours are happier and, surprisingly, just as productive. In one large trial, more than sixty companies (3) ＿＿＿＿＿ part, and most decided to keep the new system once the trial had (4) ＿＿＿＿＿ to an end. Managers reported that staff took fewer days off sick and were less (5) ＿＿＿＿＿ to leave their jobs. However, the idea does not (6) ＿＿＿＿＿ every kind of business. Hospitals and shops, for example, need people at work every day, so they would have to (7) ＿＿＿＿＿ more staff. Critics also (8) ＿＿＿＿＿ out that a shorter week can mean longer, more tiring working days.

tr.zh:
四天工作制是未來嗎？
越來越多公司在試行每週工作四天。支持者認為，工時較短的員工比較快樂，而且出乎意料地，效率一樣高。在一次大型試驗中，有六十多家公司參加，試驗結束後大多數決定保留新制度。主管們表示，員工請病假的天數變少，也比較不會離職。不過，這個做法並不適合每一種行業。例如醫院和商店每天都需要人上班，所以必須僱用更多員工。批評者也指出，每週工作天數變少，可能代表每天工作得更久、更累。

questions.zh: 「experiment with」：試行某事；test / try / prove 不和 with 這樣搭配。
「argue that …」：主張、認為；discuss / debate 後面不直接接 that 子句表示主張。
「take part」：參加。
「come to an end」：結束。
「be (less) likely to do」：（比較不）可能做某事；possible / probable 不接人當主詞加 to do。
「suit」：適合；agree 要加 with，apply 要加 to。
「employ more staff」：僱用更多員工。
「point out」：指出。

items.text:
Why do we dream?
Scientists have been trying to understand dreams (9) ＿＿＿＿＿ centuries, but there is still no single answer. One theory is that dreaming helps us to sort (10) ＿＿＿＿＿ the information we collect during the day. According (11) ＿＿＿＿＿ this idea, the brain keeps what is useful and throws away the rest. Another theory suggests that dreams allow us to practise dealing (12) ＿＿＿＿＿ dangerous situations in a safe way. (13) ＿＿＿＿＿ is clear is that almost everyone dreams, even people (14) ＿＿＿＿＿ claim they never do. Most of us simply forget our dreams within minutes of waking up, (15) ＿＿＿＿＿ we write them down immediately. So if you want to remember yours, keep a notebook next (16) ＿＿＿＿＿ your bed.

tr.zh:
我們為什麼會做夢？
科學家幾百年來一直想弄懂夢，但到現在還沒有單一的答案。有一種理論認為，做夢能幫我們整理白天收集到的資訊。根據這種說法，大腦會留下有用的、丟掉其他的。另一種理論認為，夢讓我們能在安全的情況下練習應付危險。可以確定的是，幾乎每個人都會做夢，連那些說自己從不做夢的人也一樣。我們大多只是醒來幾分鐘內就忘了夢，除非馬上寫下來。所以，如果你想記住自己的夢，就在床邊放一本筆記本吧。

questions.zh: 「for centuries」：好幾百年來；表示一段時間用 for。
questions.en: for centuries — a length of time.

questions.zh: 「sort out / sort through」：整理。
「according to」：根據。
「deal with」：處理、應付。
「What is clear is that …」：可以確定的是……
「people who claim …」：關係代名詞 who。
「unless we write them down」：除非寫下來。
「next to」：在……旁邊。

items.text:
The story of chocolate
Chocolate has a long and (17) ＿＿＿＿＿ (FASCINATE) history. The ancient peoples of Central America made a bitter drink from cocoa beans, which they believed had (18) ＿＿＿＿＿ (MAGIC) powers. When the drink arrived in Europe in the sixteenth century, it quickly became (19) ＿＿＿＿＿ (FASHION) among the rich. For a long time, however, chocolate remained a drink: the (20) ＿＿＿＿＿ (INVENT) of a way to make solid chocolate only came in the nineteenth century. Today chocolate is (21) ＿＿＿＿＿ (WIDE) available, and its (22) ＿＿＿＿＿ (POPULAR) shows no sign of falling. Some scientists even claim that dark chocolate can be (23) ＿＿＿＿＿ (BENEFIT) to our health, although others warn that eating too much of it is clearly (24) ＿＿＿＿＿ (HEALTH).

tr.zh:
巧克力的故事
巧克力有一段悠久又迷人的歷史。古代中美洲的人用可可豆做成一種苦味的飲料，他們相信它有神奇的力量。十六世紀這種飲料傳到歐洲後，很快就在有錢人之間流行起來。不過很長一段時間裡，巧克力一直是飲料；直到十九世紀，才有人發明了做出固體巧克力的方法。今天巧克力到處買得到，而且受歡迎的程度絲毫沒有下降。有些科學家甚至說黑巧克力對健康有益，但也有人警告，吃太多顯然不健康。

questions.zh: FASCINATE → fascinating（形容詞，修飾 history）。
MAGIC → magical（形容詞）；magic 也可當形容詞。
FASHION → fashionable：流行的。
INVENT → invention（名詞，the … of）。
WIDE → widely（副詞，修飾 available）。
POPULAR → popularity（名詞，its …）。
BENEFIT → beneficial：有益的（be beneficial to）。
HEALTH → unhealthy：吃太多「不健康」，要用否定字首 un-。

items.text:
(25) It wasn't necessary for you to bring a present.
      NEED
      You ＿＿＿＿＿ a present.
(26) 'I'll call you tomorrow,' Anna said to me.
      PROMISED
      Anna ＿＿＿＿＿ me the next day.
(27) I haven't seen my cousin for two years.
      LAST
      The ＿＿＿＿＿ my cousin was two years ago.
(28) It's a pity I didn't study harder.
      WISH
      I ＿＿＿＿＿ harder.
(29) People say that the castle is over 800 years old.
      SAID
      The castle ＿＿＿＿＿ over 800 years old.
(30) We couldn't play tennis because of the rain.
      PREVENTED
      The rain ＿＿＿＿＿ tennis.

tr.zh:
(25) 你不必帶禮物來。→ You ___ a present.（NEED）
(26) 安娜對我說：「我明天打給你。」→ Anna ___ me the next day.（PROMISED）
(27) 我兩年沒見到表妹了。→ The ___ my cousin was two years ago.（LAST）
(28) 可惜我當時沒更用功。→ I ___ harder.（WISH）
(29) 大家說這座城堡有八百多年歷史。→ The castle ___ over 800 years old.（SAID）
(30) 因為下雨，我們不能打網球。→ The rain ___ tennis.（PREVENTED）

questions.zh: 「didn't need to bring」或「needn't have brought」：不必帶（而且可能已經帶了）。
questions.en: didn't need to bring / needn't have brought.

questions.zh: 「promise to do」：答應要做某事；直接引語的 tomorrow 變成 the next day。
questions.en: promised to call me the next day.

questions.zh: 「The last time I saw … was two years ago」：上次見到是兩年前。
對過去的遺憾用「wish + had + 過去分詞」。
questions.en: wish I had studied — regret about the past.

questions.zh: 「be said to be」：據說是；people say that 的被動說法。
「prevent somebody from doing」：阻止某人做某事。

items.text:
My first day as a reporter
I had imagined my first day at the Evening Post many times. In my imagination I was given an important story on my first morning, and by lunchtime the editor was congratulating me on my brilliant writing. The reality was rather different.
I arrived twenty minutes early, wearing a new suit that was slightly too big for me. The receptionist looked at me as if I had come to the wrong building. 'The newsroom's on the third floor,' she said eventually, 'but nobody will be there yet.' She was right. For half an hour I sat alone among the empty desks, reading yesterday's paper and trying to look busy.
When the editor, Margaret Hughes, finally arrived, she did not seem to have been expecting me. 'Ah, the new trainee,' she said, as though she had only just remembered I existed. She handed me a list of phone numbers. 'Call these people and ask if they've seen anything unusual this week. If anyone says yes, come and tell me.'
I spent the whole morning on the phone. Most people were polite but had seen nothing; a few were annoyed to be disturbed. Then, just before one o'clock, a woman told me that a large bird had been living on the roof of the town library for three days. It sounded far too small to be news, but I wrote it down anyway.
To my surprise, Margaret was delighted. 'That's exactly the kind of thing our readers love,' she said. By the evening I was standing outside the library with a photographer, watching an enormous eagle that had escaped from a nearby wildlife park. It wasn't the story I had imagined, but it was on the front page the next day, with my name underneath.

tr.zh:
我當記者的第一天
我想像過很多次在《晚報》上班的第一天：第一個早上就拿到重要的新聞，到中午總編輯已經在稱讚我文筆出色。現實卻大不相同。
我提早二十分鐘到，穿著一套稍微太大的新西裝。櫃台小姐看我的樣子，好像我走錯了大樓。「新聞部在三樓，」她終於開口，「不過現在還沒人。」她說得沒錯。半個小時裡，我一個人坐在空蕩蕩的辦公桌之間，看著昨天的報紙，努力裝得很忙。
總編輯瑪格麗特·休斯終於來了，看起來並沒在等我。「啊，新來的實習生，」她說，好像剛剛才想起有我這個人。她遞給我一張電話號碼表：「打給這些人，問他們這週有沒有看到什麼不尋常的事。如果有人說有，就來告訴我。」
我整個上午都在打電話。大部分人很客氣，但什麼也沒看到；有幾個人被打擾還不太高興。接著，快一點的時候，一位女士告訴我，有一隻大鳥在鎮立圖書館的屋頂上住了三天。這聽起來小到根本算不上新聞，但我還是記了下來。
出乎意料，瑪格麗特非常高興：「這正是讀者喜歡的那種事。」到了晚上，我和一位攝影師站在圖書館外，看著一隻從附近野生動物園逃出來的巨大老鷹。這不是我想像中的新聞，但第二天它登上了頭版，下面署著我的名字。

questions.q: What does the writer suggest about his expectations in the first paragraph?
questions.zh: 他想像第一天就拿到重要新聞、中午就被稱讚，「現實卻大不相同」：期望不切實際。
questions.en: He imagined instant success; "the reality was rather different".

questions.q: How did the receptionist react when he arrived?
options: She seemed surprised to see him.
She took him to the newsroom.
She told him he was late.
questions.zh: 「看我的樣子，好像我走錯了大樓」：她很意外。
questions.en: She looked as if he had come to the wrong building.

questions.q: The editor's words 'Ah, the new trainee' suggest that she
options: had almost forgotten he was starting.
questions.zh: 「好像剛剛才想起有我這個人」：她差點忘了他今天開始上班。
questions.en: As though she had only just remembered he existed.

questions.q: What was he asked to do in the morning?
questions.zh: 總編輯要他「打給這些人，問他們這週有沒有看到什麼不尋常的事」。
questions.en: Call people and ask about anything unusual.

questions.q: How did he feel about the woman's information?
options: He doubted it was important enough.
He was sure it would be on the front page.
He thought she was not telling the truth.
He was annoyed that she had called.
questions.zh: 「聽起來小到根本算不上新聞」：他懷疑它不夠重要。
questions.en: It sounded far too small to be news.

options: His story appeared on the front page.
The eagle flew back to the park.
He was given a different story.
questions.zh: 「第二天它登上了頭版，下面署著我的名字」。
questions.en: It was on the front page with his name.

items.text:
Running my first marathon
Two years ago I could barely run for a bus. Last month I finished the London Marathon. (37) ＿＿＿＿＿ It started with a bet. A colleague said I would never manage to run five kilometres, so I signed up for a local fun run to prove him wrong.
The first few weeks of training were miserable. (38) ＿＿＿＿＿ My legs ached, I was always out of breath, and I seriously considered giving up.
Things changed when I joined a running club. (39) ＿＿＿＿＿ Running with other people made a huge difference, partly because we encouraged each other and partly because I didn't want to be the one who stopped first.
By the following spring I had completed a half marathon, and someone suggested I should try the full distance. (40) ＿＿＿＿＿ But once the idea was in my head, I couldn't forget it.
Training for a marathon takes over your life. (41) ＿＿＿＿＿ My weekends disappeared into long runs, and I had to say no to a lot of parties.
On the day itself, the crowds were incredible. (42) ＿＿＿＿＿ When I finally crossed the finish line, after four and a half hours, I didn't know whether to laugh or cry.
bank: I laughed at first, because it seemed completely impossible.
Strangers shouted my name, which I'd written on my shirt, and it kept me going.
I still can't quite believe it.
I went out three times a week, but I never seemed to get any faster.
For four months, I ran five or six times a week.
The members were friendly, and nobody cared how slow I was.
My colleague was the first to congratulate me on finishing the fun run.

tr.zh:
我的第一場馬拉松
兩年前，我連追公車都跑不動。上個月，我跑完了倫敦馬拉松。我到現在還不太敢相信。這一切始於一個打賭：一位同事說我連五公里都跑不完，所以我報名了當地的趣味路跑，想證明他錯了。
剛開始訓練的幾個星期很痛苦。我一週跑三次，卻好像怎麼也跑不快。腿痠、老是喘不過氣，我認真考慮過放棄。
加入跑步社以後，情況變了。社員都很友善，沒有人在意我跑得多慢。和別人一起跑差別很大，一方面我們互相打氣，一方面我也不想當第一個停下來的人。
到了隔年春天，我跑完了一場半馬，有人建議我試試全馬。一開始我笑了，因為那看起來完全不可能。可是這個念頭一進到腦子裡，就再也忘不掉。
準備馬拉松會佔據你的生活。四個月裡，我每週跑五、六次。週末都消失在長跑裡，很多派對也只好推掉。
比賽當天，觀眾多得驚人。陌生人喊著我寫在衣服上的名字，讓我撐了下去。花了四個半小時終於跨過終點線時，我不知道該笑還是該哭。

questions.zh: 前面說跑完了倫敦馬拉松，接著「我到現在還不太敢相信」。
questions.en: After finishing the marathon: "I still can't quite believe it."

questions.zh: 訓練很痛苦：一週跑三次卻跑不快，接著說腿痠、想放棄。
questions.en: Miserable training: no faster, aching legs.

questions.zh: 加入跑步社：社員很友善，接著說和別人一起跑差別很大。
questions.en: The club: friendly members, running together helped.

questions.zh: 有人建議跑全馬，他「一開始笑了」；後面的 But 說念頭還是忘不掉。
questions.en: He laughed at first — "But" the idea stayed.

questions.zh: 準備馬拉松佔據生活：四個月每週跑五、六次，週末都在長跑。
questions.en: Training took over: five or six runs a week.

questions.zh: 觀眾很多：陌生人喊他的名字讓他撐下去。G（同事恭喜他跑完趣味路跑）放哪裡都不合，是多出來的。
questions.en: The crowds shouted his name. G is the extra sentence.

bank: Lily, 19 — I started selling handmade jewellery online when I was sixteen. My parents weren't convinced it was a good idea; they thought I should be concentrating on my exams. Now I have three people working for me. My advice? Listen to your customers. Every new design I make starts with something a customer has asked for.

Omar, 22 — At university I was shocked by how much textbooks cost, so I created an app for students to swap them. My first version was a disaster — nobody could work out how to use it — and I nearly gave up. Luckily an investor saw the second version and offered to support me.

Grace, 24 — I opened a vegan bakery with money I borrowed from my grandmother. I start at four in the morning and rarely finish before eight in the evening, but I love it. Next year I'm hoping to open a second shop on the other side of the city.

Ben, 21 — I repair old bikes and sell them again, mainly because I hate seeing things thrown away when they could still be used. I work from my parents' garage, and on Saturdays I run workshops where I teach people to fix their own bikes.

tr.zh:
A 莉莉（19 歲）：我十六歲開始在網路上賣手工飾品。爸媽一開始不太看好，覺得我應該專心準備考試。現在我有三個員工。我的建議是：聽客人的話。我每一個新設計都是從客人的要求開始的。
B 奧馬（22 歲）：大學時我被課本的價格嚇到，所以做了一個讓學生交換課本的應用程式。第一版很失敗，沒人搞得懂怎麼用，我差點放棄。幸好有一位投資人看到第二版，願意支持我。
C 葛蕾絲（24 歲）：我向奶奶借錢開了一家純素烘焙坊。我凌晨四點開工，很少晚上八點前收工，但我很喜歡。明年我希望在城市的另一頭開第二家店。
D 班（21 歲）：我修理舊腳踏車再賣出去，主要是因為我討厭看到還能用的東西被丟掉。我在爸媽的車庫工作，每個星期六開工作坊，教大家自己修車。

questions.q: Which person says their family was not sure about their plans at first?
questions.zh: 莉莉的「爸媽一開始不太看好」。

questions.q: Which person had a first attempt that failed?
questions.zh: 奧馬的「第一版很失敗」。
questions.en: Omar: the first version was a disaster.

questions.q: Which person is motivated by concern for the environment?
questions.zh: 班「討厭看到還能用的東西被丟掉」。
questions.en: Ben hates things being thrown away.

questions.q: Which person got financial help from a relative?
questions.zh: 葛蕾絲「向奶奶借錢」。

questions.q: Which person got their idea from a problem they had themselves?
questions.zh: 奧馬自己被課本價格嚇到，才做了交換課本的程式。
questions.en: Omar was shocked by textbook prices.

questions.q: Which person teaches skills to other people?
questions.zh: 班「每個星期六開工作坊，教大家自己修車」。

questions.q: Which person works very long days?
questions.zh: 葛蕾絲凌晨四點開工，很少晚上八點前收工。
questions.en: Grace works from 4 a.m. to 8 p.m.

questions.zh: 莉莉「現在有三個員工」。
questions.en: Lily has three people working for her.

questions.q: Which person hopes to expand their business?
questions.zh: 葛蕾絲希望明年開第二家店。

questions.q: Which person believes that paying attention to customers is essential?
questions.zh: 莉莉的建議：「聽客人的話」。
